job.title: Marketing Operations Manager
job.description:
Marketing Operations Manager - 12 Month Contract

Global Tech Business

$169.5K + Super

Our client is a global technology company at the forefront of creative and digital marketing software, with a significant presence across international markets and a growing footprint across APAC. The organisation invests heavily in data driven marketing operations and operates through collaborative, globally distributed teams. This role offers genuine international exposure and the chance to work alongside senior leaders across multiple regions.

About the Role:

We are seeking an experienced Marketing Operations Manager to lead the APAC marketing planning cadence and drive budget management excellence across the region. Based in Sydney, you will sit within a globally distributed International Strategy and Operations team, working closely with international colleagues to align planning, budgeting and reporting across APAC. It is an initial 12 month contract with strong potential to extend, or potentially convert to Perm.

Key Duties:

  • Own and manage the APAC marketing planning cadence, including State of Readiness, leadership alignment sessions, strategic briefing weeks, budget reviews and cross-functional all-hands.
  • Lead quarterly rolling forecasts and annual budget planning using Anaplan, in partnership with global stakeholders.
  • Manage APAC marketing budgets, covering both variable and centrally owned spend, alongside the International Budget Lead.
  • Track and report on marketing spend using Power BI dashboards, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency and reduce cost.
  • Maintain and standardise foundational planning documents for APAC and drive adoption of consistent planning and operating models across the region.

Key Requirements:

  • Proven experience in marketing operations, strategy and operations, or a similar function, ideally within a large, matrixed global organisation.
  • Hands-on budget management and financial planning experience, with proficiency in Anaplan or a comparable planning platform.
  • Demonstrated ability to coordinate stakeholders across time zones and manage complex, multi-market operating rhythms.
  • Strong data driven reporting skills, with comfort using Power BI dashboards or similar tools.
  • Excellent senior-level communication skills, with the ability to distil complexity into clear, actionable insights.
  • Sydney based, with the ability to meet a 50% in-office expectation and flexibility for recurring evening calls with international teams.
  • Experience in technology or SaaS environments, and within global enterprise organisations, is highly regarded.

How to Apply:

If this sounds like the opportunity you have been waiting for, we would love to hear from you, so apply now to find out more.

job.title: Senior Engineer
job.description:
Senior IP Networking Engineer
Sydney – Rosebery | Onsite with free parking | Full-time permanent role

  • Senior IP networking engineer role with a genuine, longer-term path to team leadership
  • Hands-on technical role built on TCP/UDP, VLANs, multicast and PTP, Cisco a bonus
  • Sydney based, working across APAC for a global leader in broadcast and live event tech


We are working exclusively with a world-leading business whose products are used in high-end, large-scale events. Their technology is trusted on the world's biggest stages across broadcast, live events, pro-audio, sports, theatre, and security applications. And despite their global reach, they've retained a local, family feel to their operations in Sydney.

About the Role

This is a Sydney-based, senior technical role supporting APAC customers on complex IP networking issues within broadcast and live event technology, spanning TCP/UDP, VLANs, multicast and PTP. The role is genuinely hands-on: you will work directly on the trickier technical cases and act as a point of escalation, while mentoring and supporting other engineers across the APAC team.

Duties

  • Provide hands-on technical support on complex customer cases involving IP networking, including TCP/UDP, VLANs, multicast and PTP.
  • Mentor and support engineers across the APAC team, sharing technical expertise and helping resolve escalated issues.
  • Step in on sensitive customer relationship matters, such as billing disputes or SLA concerns, as they arise.
  • Build familiarity with the team's case follow-up discipline and customer engagement processes through Salesforce.
  • Travel periodically to regional offices and training events

Requirements

  • Strong, hands-on foundation in IT/IP networking, including TCP/UDP, VLANs, multicast and PTP; Cisco knowledge highly regarded.
  • Background in broadcast, pro-audio or media/OT technology.
  • A Principal Engineer, Senior Engineer or Technical Lead background, with genuine mentoring experience valued; a formal "Manager" title is not required.
  • Comfortable working within a team spread across different cultural contexts, particularly across the Asia-Pacific region, with openness to growing into people leadership over time.
  • A hands-on, proactive approach.
  • CRM experience, particularly Salesforce, is an advantage
  • Full working rights in Australia

job.title: Head of ICT
job.description:
About the client

Our client is a well-established, publicly funded Sydney cultural institution with a history stretching back to the early nineteenth century, recognised as one of the country's most significant scientific and heritage organisations. Operating within the NSW public sector, it balances a strong public engagement mandate with a substantial collection, research and exhibition program. Behind the exhibits sits a busy operational environment, where ICT service delivery, cyber security and end-user computing all underpin the organisation's day-to-day work. The organisation is now looking for additional ICT leadership capacity to support an established team through a defined period.

About the role

This is a hands-on, people-focused ICT leadership role, brought in to keep day-to-day service delivery running smoothly for a defined period. You will take charge of an existing ICT team, providing direct people management, coaching and performance oversight, while overseeing service assurance, support and end-user computing standards across the organisation. The scope is deliberately practical: this role is about operational delivery and team leadership rather than project ownership or budget sign-off, giving you a clear mandate without the weight of strategic decision-making. It is a six-month contract suited to an experienced operator who wants to make an immediate impact within a well-regarded organisation.

Duties

  • Manage the day-to-day functional delivery of ICT services, including service assurance, performance and availability.
  • Lead and support the existing ICT team, including direct coaching and performance conversations with staff.
  • Oversee end-user computing support and maintenance across the organisation.
  • Apply cyber security best practice across day-to-day ICT operations.
  • Review and recommend on matters that would normally require sign-off, escalating decisions to the appropriate approval authority.

Requirements

  • Proven experience managing the day-to-day functional delivery of ICT services, including service assurance, performance and support.
  • Demonstrated people management experience, including direct coaching and performance conversations with staff.
  • Minimum five years' experience in the implementation, transformation and support of end-user computing environments.
  • Working knowledge of cyber security best practices.
  • Comfortable operating in a review-and-recommend capacity, without full sign-off authority.
  • Public sector, NSW government or cultural institution experience highly regarded.

How to apply

If this sounds like the kind of assignment where you can make an immediate, hands-on difference, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Data Engineer / Data Architect – Databricks & AWS
job.description:
TECHNICAL LEAD / PRINCIPAL ENGINEER / HANDS-ON ARCHITECT - DATA ENGINEERING (PLATFORM & INFRASTRUCTURE)

Sydney, NSW (on-site) | Full Australian working rights required - we're unable to progress candidates without them.

You've built a Databricks and AWS data platform from nothing before: medallion architecture, Delta Lake, real pipelines and real tradeoffs, not a diagram someone else handed you. If that's familiar, keep reading. Sydney-based, Technical Lead through to Hands-on Architect, genuinely hands-on at every level.

SEEK SELLING POINTS

  • You've built a platform from nothing before. This role needs that again.
  • Haven't led a team yet? If you're ready to, this is where you start.
  • Join a 500+ strong data and AI practice, backed by tier-one vendor alliances.

ABOUT THE CLIENT

A top-tier global professional services firm delivering large-scale data and AI transformation programs for major enterprise and government clients across Australia. This is deep, complex platform and infrastructure build work, not light analytics or reporting. You get total ownership of the platforms you build, structured investment in advanced technical training, and direct access to the vendors behind the stack, not just a licence and a support ticket.

ABOUT THE TEAM

You'd be joining a data and AI practice of 500+ specialist practitioners nationally, sitting inside tier-one vendor alliances spanning AWS, Databricks, Google Cloud, dbt Labs, Snowflake, Salesforce and Informatica. The programs here run at genuine scale: think large transport-network digital twin builds, national-scale public health rollout automation, and sustainability data initiatives delivered across Australia and the wider region. Career development is coaching-led, with benefits including dedicated wellbeing leave, paid volunteering and market-leading parental leave.

ABOUT THE ROLE

If you've built a data platform from the ground up before, you already know the difference between that and being handed one to extend. This is the first kind. You'll be designing and building end-to-end Databricks Lakehouse platforms including medallion architecture, batch and streaming pipelines, and Delta Lake at the core, backed by AWS (Glue or Redshift), not a single layer someone else designed around you.

How much of that you own depends on where you sit, and leadership experience isn't a prerequisite at every level. As a Technical Lead, you might already be leading a team, or you might be ready to step into that for the first time with real support behind you. As a Principal Engineer or Hands-on Architect, you're setting technical direction and coaching engineers through the complexity yourself. Either way, you own the platform, not a slice of it.

DUTIES

  • Architect end-to-end Databricks Lakehouse platforms, including medallion architecture, on AWS (Glue or Redshift).
  • Design and build batch, streaming and real-time pipelines feeding AI and advanced analytics workloads.
  • Own distributed systems performance: Spark tuning, query optimisation, and cost and cluster right-sizing at scale.
  • Improve CI/CD, infrastructure as code (Terraform) and automated deployment practice across the platform.
  • Technical Lead level: own delivery of your components directly, whether you're already leading others or ready to step into that for the first time.
  • Principal Engineer / Hands-on Architect level: set technical direction across the build and coach engineers through the complexity, not just review their output.
  • Get direct access to advanced vendor training and close working relationships with the platform partners behind the stack.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Proven experience building data platforms end to end, infrastructure through to data lake, not one layer in isolation.
  • Deep hands-on Databricks and Delta Lake, including medallion architecture and PySpark or Scala, with AWS (Glue or Redshift at minimum).
  • Advanced SQL and performance tuning across distributed systems, with real Spark and cloud troubleshooting experience.
  • Databricks certifications (Certified Data Engineer / Certified Professional) and AWS certifications highly regarded, not mandatory.
  • Technical Lead level: strong individual delivery on complex builds. Prior leadership experience is valued but not required, clear potential to lead is enough.
  • Principal Engineer / Hands-on Architect level: demonstrated ownership of technical direction and coaching engineers through delivery, not just managing tickets.
  • Comfortable in genuine ambiguity on large, complex programs, not tightly scoped analytics or reporting projects.
  • Full Australian working rights required. We are unable to progress applications without them.

HOW TO APPLY

If the platforms you've built, or are ready to lead, are the reason people call you when things go wrong, we should talk.Send me your CV!!

KEY SKILLS

Databricks, Delta Lake, Apache Spark, PySpark, Scala, Medallion Architecture, AWS, Glue, Redshift, Terraform, CI/CD, Data Engineering, Data Architecture, Data Platform, Data Lake, Sydney.

A note from the consultant running this search: I've placed engineers into this practice who came in as builders and ended up leading their own workstreams within a year. The ones who thrive aren't chasing a title, they're chasing the platform work that's actually hard. If your CV reads like tidy dashboards and light reporting, this isn't your role. If it reads like you've fought with Spark cluster configs at 11pm and won, let's talk.

job.title: Customer Service Consultant
job.description:
Customer Service Consultant
Kitchen Hardware Showroom
$75k - $80k + Super
UNDERWOOD, QLD - 4119
Permanent - Full-time
On-site role (Monday – Friday 9 – 5 only)

Cox Purtell is currently working with a world-renowned, family-owned global leader in functional furniture fittings, who are seeking a dedicated and customer-focused individual to join their team as a Showroom Consultant. Their products are trusted in kitchens and homes around the world, and as a family-owned company, they place a genuine emphasis on their people, offering real opportunities for career growth and development within a global organisation.

Role Overview:
Reporting to the State Sales Manager, as Showroom Consultant you would plan and deliver marketing and sales activities to grow the product range within their showroom market. It's a great fit for someone with a retail, trade counter or customer service background, perhaps from a hardware, kitchen supply or similar showroom environment, who enjoys a hands-on, customer-facing role.

Duties include but are not limited to:

Customer Support:

  • Responsible for greeting customers and supporting them through their visit at the Showroom.
  • Responsible for answering incoming calls in a timely and professional manner.
  • Responsible for maintaining customer/visitor registration database.

Skills & Experience:

  • Well-developed inter-personal skills.
  • Solid organization skills.
  • Ability to work well with others.
  • Problem solving and time management skills.
  • Effective verbal, presentation and listening communications skills.
  • Effective written communications skills.

Why Apply?

  • Be part of a world-renowned, family-owned company with a strong focus on people, quality and values.
  • Work with a dynamic team committed to delivering exceptional customer service.
  • If you're a customer-focused individual with a passion for providing outstanding service and technical support, we want to hear from you! Apply now and become a part of the team.

job.title: Field Sales Representative

Sales Representative – Stairlift & Accessibility Solutions

  • Sydney Inner West

If this sounds like the high-growth sales opportunity you have been looking for, we would love to hear from you.

job.title: Operations & Membership Officer
job.description:
Are you an experienced association or B2B professional looking for a role where you can genuinely shape the growth of a peak industry body? My client, a national association representing suppliers of packaging and processing automation, technology and equipment, is looking for an Operations & Membership Officer to help drive their member and industry services forward.

The organisation runs industry-leading events, including a flagship triennial trade exhibition, alongside a strong member services and partnerships program. With over 150 Australian-based company members, this is a genuinely varied role working closely with the General Manager, CEO and business partners across the full operations of the association.

What you'll be doing:

  • Proactively identifying, targeting and converting new member companies to drive satisfaction, retention and growth.
  • Coordinating the association's presence at domestic and international trade events, from stand design and staffing through to marketing and lead follow-up.
  • Building and nurturing relationships with sponsors and service partners, and pitching new partners that resonate with the membership.
  • Driving member communications across newsletters, LinkedIn, forums and other digital channels, including publications and member content.
  • Delivering clear, timely reporting on acquisition, sponsorship revenue, event performance and marketing engagement.
  • Managing the association's recurring events calendar, including its flagship exhibition, an annual awards program, and other member gatherings.

What we're looking for:

  • 5+ years' experience in a customer-facing, coordination or business operations role (association, events or B2B environment preferred).
  • Experience in an industry association or membership organisation.
  • Strong relationship management and communication skills.
  • Ability to work autonomously and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • High proficiency with CRM/member database systems, MS Office Suite and cloud-based platforms.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills in a professional context.

Great to have (not essential):

  • Background in events coordination or trade exhibition delivery.
  • Exposure to sponsorship or partnership management.
  • Familiarity with the packaging, processing or broader manufacturing sector.

This is a fantastic opportunity for a relationship-driven operator who wants genuine variety, autonomy and the chance to play a key role in the continued success of a peak industry body.

Salary is competitive and commensurate with experience, circa $90,000 to $100,000 plus superannuation, with interstate and occasional international travel a few times a year.

job.title: AEM Customer Success Manager
job.description:
AEM Customer Success Manager

About the client

Our client is a global software company whose digital experience products sit behind some of the most recognisable brands and websites in the world. Their APAC Customer Success team works with a large enterprise portfolio, helping organisations get genuine commercial return from significant technology investments. The culture is collaborative, data-informed and genuinely customer-obsessed, with the scale and structure you would expect from a major multinational and the autonomy to shape how you work. This is a permanent role based in Sydney CBD with hybrid working.

About the role

As a Solutions Customer Success Manager you will act as the trusted advisor across a portfolio of enterprise customers, working in a dynamic one-to-many model through fixed-scope engagements. Your focus is adoption and value: quickly pinpointing where a customer is underusing their solutions, running the engagement that closes that gap, and evidencing the outcome in a value summary co-owned with your stakeholders. You will work across the enterprise book of business to reach the customers who need help most, ideally before they know they need it. It is a role for someone who enjoys deep product expertise, commercial conversations and the pace of moving between engagements rather than sitting on a single account.

Duties

      • Own overall customer success across an enterprise portfolio, driving feature adoption, improving customer health and evidencing confirmed value delivered.
      • Scope and deliver fixed-timeframe engagements, identifying specific areas of improvement and executing against them within the agreed scope.
      • Align engagement outcomes to value summaries co-owned with key customer stakeholders, so customer value and commercial value move together.
      • Run customer workshops and advisory sessions that showcase best practice and new ways to extend digital maturity across the product suite.
      • Analyse adoption data and customer feedback to spot patterns, recommend improvements and surface areas of unmet demand, then feed that intelligence back internally as the voice of the customer.

Requirements

      • Five or more years of relevant experience, ideally across digital or experience marketing, content management or customer journey management.
      • Two or more years of hands-on solution expertise with Adobe Technology in AEM sites and AEM assets including EDS.
      • Background in a large SaaS environment or another major multinational, working with enterprise-scale customers.
      • Working knowledge of AI and agent capabilities, with content supply chain and modern delivery architecture exposure highly regarded.
      • Proven track record as a trusted advisor, translating product capability into business ROI and measurable customer value.
      • Consulting or business consulting experience, with the commercial mindset to hold value conversations at a senior level.
      • Strong stakeholder and interpersonal skills, including the ability to navigate and mediate conflict and build durable partnerships.
      • Ability to prioritise across multiple concurrent engagements and perform effectively under pressure.
      • Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills.
      • Flexibility to travel approximately 20% of the time.
      • Bachelor's or master's degree.
      • Full Australian working rights.

How to apply

If this sounds like the next step for you, we would love to hear from you, so please apply with an up to date CV for immediate consideration.

job.title: Accountant
job.description:
Project Accountant
Full-time permanent role
Redfern (WFH flexibility) | Full time | $90,000–$100,000 + super

  • Redfern with genuine work-from-home flexibility offered
  • Own end-to-end project finance for a fast-growing creative agency across Sydney and APAC
  • Hands-on, varied role offering real autonomy and close exposure to production teams daily

About the client

Our client is a dynamic, fast-growing agency with a well-established presence across the Asia-Pacific region, including offices in Sydney and Singapore. Known for delivering high-quality creative and production work for a diverse portfolio of clients, the business has built a reputation for commercial rigour paired with a genuinely collaborative culture. Finance sits close to the action here, partnering directly with Producers and Account Leads rather than operating at arm's length. It is a business that values precision, integrity and strong working relationships as much as the numbers themselves.

About the role

This is a hands-on, commercially focused role for a Project Accountant ready to take ownership of the full financial lifecycle of projects, from revenue recognition and billing through to job costing and final reconciliations. Reporting to the APAC Controller and working closely with Producers and Account Leads, you will become the financial backbone behind projects delivered across Sydney and Singapore. Based in Redfern with the flexibility to work from home, this role offers genuine variety, autonomy and the opportunity to make a visible commercial impact within a close-knit, supportive finance team.

Duties

  • Own project job costing, setting up vendors and maintaining accurate project costs across operating and finance systems.
  • Review and match purchase orders and vendor invoices against project budgets and deliverables, monitoring PO closures ahead of final reconciliation.
  • Manage vendor and freelancer onboarding and compliance across the APAC region, including Certificates of Insurance, Master Service Agreements, rate cards and Scopes of Work.
  • Oversee the APAC accounts payable and receivable function, including invoice processing, aging management, weekly payment runs and supplier reconciliations.
  • Support month-end close by performing bank reconciliations, processing general journals and assisting with GL reconciliations.

Requirements

  • Accounting degree or equivalent qualification.
  • 3–5 years' accounting experience, ideally with a focus on agency finance or project accounting.
  • Strong Excel skills and proficiency with accounting software; experience with Procim is highly regarded.
  • Solid understanding of GST compliance requirements across Australia and Singapore.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, with a demonstrated ability to build strong relationships with producers, account managers and external vendors.
  • A self-motivated, proactive problem solver comfortable prioritising across multiple projects and dynamic teams.

How to apply

If you're a commercially minded accountant who thrives on ownership, variety and being close to the action, we would love to hear from you.
